assertions.subject: Dementia
assertions.quote: Prevalence of the disease doubles every five years beyond the age of sixty-five.

assertions.subject: Alzheimer's disease
assertions.quote: AD belongs to this first group and is the leading cause of dementia, accounting for fifty to seventy percent of all dementia cases.

assertions.subject: Vascular dementia
assertions.quote: VaD which represents approximately twenty percent of all dementias, making it the second leading cause of the syndrome.

assertions.subject: Neurodegenerative disease
assertions.quote: The former are known as neurodegenerative since they constitute dementia as a clinical manifestation.

assertions.subject: Dementia with Lewy bodies
assertions.quote: Dementia with Lewy bodies and frontal-temporal lobe degeneration are also part of this group.

assertions.subject: Frontal-temporal lobe degeneration
assertions.quote: Dementia with Lewy bodies and frontal-temporal lobe degeneration are also part of this group.

assertions.subject: Parkinson’s disease
assertions.quote: The primary dementias also include those in which dementia is set to become the main clinical manifestation. Such examples include Parkinson’s disease, Huntington’s disease and progressive supranuclear palsy.
